chunks: Therefore, He has appreciated their actions and praised their position.
They call Him and breathe in the air of forgiveness, they are ever needy of His bounty and remain humble before His greatness,
The length of their grief has pained their hearts, and the length of weeping their eyes.
They knock at every door of inclination towards Allāh.
They ask Him Whom generosity does not make destitute and from Whom those who approach Him do not get disappointed.
Therefore, take account of yourself for your own sake because the account of others will be taken by one other than you.

key_terms.حَسِيبٌ: Accountant or one who takes account
key_terms.رَهَائِنُ: Pledges or hostages (metaphor for being held in need)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of supplication and self-accountability in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this passage from the Exegesis of Surah An-Nur, Imam Ali (AS) portrays the supplicants as captives of their own humility, whose tears and longing serve as collateral for God's boundless generosity. He emphasizes that their persistent hope is never in vain, as they call upon the One whose resources are inexhaustible. The passage concludes with a profound spiritual principle: while we are personally accountable for our own deeds, we must also recognize that others bear responsibility for their own souls, reinforcing the concept of individual accountability (Hisab) in Shia theology.
